claims.claim: Le Guin told Paul Morton that she loves the sound of language and plays with word sounds in her head.

claims.claim: Le Guin said she does not write dialogue the way Hemingway writes Spanish-accented English in For Whom the Bell Tolls, and that she finds it a little affected and foolish.

coverage: ROSTER (13 named items). FETCHED: Adam Roberts (his blog sibilantfricative is now private — live search page and the Blogger feed API both return "User does not have permission to read this blog" — so his Le Guin criticism was read as the Adam's Notebook Medium essay on A Wizard of Earthsea via Wayback raw, medium.com live being 403 and scribe.rip 404); Sean Guynes's Reactor reread (four entries read live — Tombs of Atuan, The Farthest Shore, Very Far Away from Anywhere Else, Tehanu — found by search and link because the /series/ index returns 403; the leguin-craft-raw2/guynes-tombs.txt already on disk is a Wayback "not archived" stub); Erlich's Coyote's Song (nine further chapters via Wayback raw 20151107114510id_, sfra.org being dead); the five video essays (SEVEN read, as auto-caption transcripts pulled with youtube-transcript-api after the in-page timedtext URL returned empty without a signature — James Marino's "Le Guin's Style" and Philip Chase on "From Elfland to Poughkeepsie" are the two substantive ones); Jo Walton (two further Reactor entries); Paradoxa 21 table of contents. ALREADY DONE BY THE PREDECESSOR and not repeated: Atwood's "Queen of Quinkdom" and 2018 Guardian tribute, Mitchell, Phillips, Walton's Tehanu and Atuan essays, Kirkus's Tehanu review, Craig, the two Library of America pages, the NYT obituary, Dirda, Kelso's Paradoxa introduction. BLOCKED: the Reddit threads (old.reddit .json redirects to a login wall, www.reddit.com .json returns 403 under a browser UA, a redlib mirror returns 403, and WebFetch refuses reddit.com); Atwood's In Other Worlds (the archive.org copy is lending-restricted and its search-inside endpoint returns 403 — and its Le Guin chapter is the reprinted Quinkdom essay already read); the rest of Paradoxa 21 (per-article paywall, incl. Amy Clarke's "Tales from the Distaff" and Le Guin's own "Living in a Work of Art"); T. A. Shippey's "The Magic Art and the Evolution of Words" (OUP 403) and the 2010 Children's Literature names article (Project MUSE bot challenge) — Shippey is the single biggest remaining gap for this angle. EXPANSION: bibliography chasing through ursulakleguin.com's interview and review indexes gave The Millions (Paul Morton), Hari Kunzru in The Guardian, Jonathan White, Electric Literature, David Naimon at Lit Hub and Jason P. Vest at The Common Reader; Crossref/OpenAlex gave Amenta's Polish-translation paper (open access, line-level) and Ozgun's Turkish paper; lateral searches gave Swanwick, Burt on Plotz, and chapter 1 of Steering the Craft published in full at Lit Hub. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-run (200/200), so the last three discovery passes ran on link-chasing and Crossref/OpenAlex alone; the final two passes surfaced nothing substantive beyond Naimon and Vest. THIS RUN: 56 source entries logged, 33 of them substantive reads, 93 new claims, every quotation string re-verified by exact substring match against the fetched text before each of the five checkpoint writes (0 blanked). Totals in sweep/found-leguin-close-2.json, including the predecessor's checkpoint: 73 sources, 159 claims.
